structure.heading: Benchmarking Baseline: Cycle Time, First-Pass Yield, and Capacity Utilisation Across Plants
text_content: **Benchmarking Baseline: Cycle Time, First-Pass Yield, and Capacity Utilisation Across Plants**

Baseline operational data were collected from 2026-01-01 to 2026-03-31 across Plants A, B, and C to establish a common benchmarking dataset. Data elements captured included Order-to-Ship cycle time, process-stage cycle times, first-pass yield, and capacity utilisation at line and plant level. Collection used standardized timestamping, audit logs, and production reports consolidated in the central analytics repository. This consistent window enables direct comparisons across entities, normalizes for weekly cadence, and supports time-bound performance trending for the subsequent improvement prioritisation activities analysis.

Cycle-time benchmarking highlighted material divergence: Plant B median Order-to-Ship cycle time is 9.6 days versus Plant A at 6.2 days, indicating a 54% longer throughput interval at Plant B on median. Detailed stage analysis revealed extended queue times and handoff delays at outbound staging and scheduling synchronization issues. Priorities for diagnostic work include lead-time breakdowns by workstation, percentage time spent waiting, and cross-functional scheduling alignment. These findings inform targeted lean interventions to reduce non-value wait and improve on-time fulfilment rates.

Quality and utilisation metrics completed the baseline: Plant C first-pass yield is 92.4% versus Plant A at 97.1%, identifying higher rework and scrap exposure at Plant C and quantifying defect-related throughput loss. Capacity utilisation assessments showed differing effective utilisation rates by line, driven by downtime patterns, changeover frequency, and demand mix. Recommended actions include defect root-cause tracing, setup reduction programs, and targeted preventive maintenance to raise first-pass yield and available capacity. Financial and operational impacts will be modeled against baseline.

structure.heading: Lean Opportunity Portfolio and 12-Month Financial Impact Projection
text_content: **Lean Opportunity Portfolio and 12-Month Financial Impact Projection**

The lean opportunity portfolio prioritises targeted operational improvements to deliver measurable outcomes at Plant B. Key target: a 1.8-day cycle-time reduction for Plant B Order-to-Ship within 12 months, achieved through takt realignment, line balancing, and quick-change initiatives on critical flows. Execution ownership rests with the Operations Excellence Program Office and Plant B leadership.

Financial modelling projects $3.4M in annualised savings against a one-time implementation cost of $0.9M, yielding first-year net benefit of $2.5M. The largest single initiative, SMED on Line 2, contributes $1.2M of the annualised savings; the balance ($2.2M) is allocated across efficiency, yield, and capacity projects. Estimated simple payback is ~3.2 months (0.27 years).

Implementation will run from May 2026 to May 2027 with staged milestones at 3, 6, 9 and 12 months. Governance is led by the Operations Excellence Program Office with oversight from the Continuous Improvement Council; KPIs tracked weekly include Order-to-Ship cycle-time, first-pass yield, capacity utilisation, and realised cost savings. Sensitivity analysis models a ±15% variance in savings to inform contingency planning.
